thread:
nightly-bot: [ALERT] pset_v27 nightly eval: 6.2% failure increase on 'date-normalization' suite vs baseline. See /evals/2026/pset_v27/summary

mel: ugh saw this on wake-up. pset v27 landed yesterday with a wording tweak. failing mostly on relative-date cases.

kai: can you paste an example failing case?

mel: sure — prompt + model output vs expected:
```
Prompt: 'Convert to ISO date: the first of August last year'
Expected: '2023-08-01'
Model(v3-q4): 'Aug 1st, 2023'
```

mel: the eval checker treats that as mismatch (we only accept YYYY-MM-DD).

anya: did the pset change change the label format or the prompt wording?

mel: wording tweak: we rephrased some prompts from "first of August last year" -> "the first day of August last year" to improve clarity. not sure why outputs differ.

tom: two quick hypotheses — tokenization/quantization drift on q4 build OR the model variant used by nightly switched to a different decode config (temp/penalties). i can run targeted ablation.

linda: can we diff the pset v26->v27? maybe a subtle rewording caused model to favor month-name vs numeric.

mel: attaching small diff from CI: - "first of August" + "the first day of August" (plus one extra example where we removed "(in ISO)" hint).

kai: removing explicit hint could explain it. previously many prompts had "(in ISO)" which biased numeric output.

anya: i'd rather not revert the whole set. two options: rebaseline expected outputs to accept alternate formats, or restore the explicit ISO hint in prompts. need ML lead approval for rebaseline. @anya please confirm.

anya: quick triage plan: 1) run local evals on v3 and v3-q4 quantized to compare 2) check nightly config for decode/cosmetics 3) generate a small canary set and push canary rollout 4) if pattern is consistent, propose rebaseline PR with accepted-format regex.

mel: running local eval now on both variants, will post numbers in ~10m.

nightly-bot: run 2015000100 - pset_v27 subset run started (canary subset=200 examples)

tom: FYI i reproduced the month-name vs numeric pattern on q4 quantized locally. v3 fp32 still prefers numeric. quantization seems correlated.

linda: good catch. so we might need quant-sensitive rebaseline. that means two rebaseline PRs? ugh.

kai: alternatively, update the checker to accept both numeric and month-name for relative dates (regex) — lower risk and quicker. but need evaluation: does accepting both increase false positives?

anya: agree with kai. create PR to relax the checker for this pset category, add note in rebaseline docs that q4 differs for non-critical formatting. I'll sign off if tests pass.

mel: opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/psets/pull/482 — description: "pset_v27: update date-normalization checker to accept month-name and ISO numeric; add canary notes for quantized variants"

mel: tagging owners: @anya @linda for approval. :eyes:

linda: quick skim looks fine. can we add one golden-case to ensure we still enforce strict ISO when prompt includes '(in ISO)'?

mel: added test. pushed.

tom: after PR merged please schedule a nightly re-run on canary. i'll prepare a short note in the rebaseline log about q4 behavior.

anya: sounds like plan — will review and approve PR after CI.

mel: thanks all. summary: not a model bug per se, interaction between prompt wording and quantized variant; short-term: relax checker + add tests; medium-term: consider restoring explicit ISO hints where format strictness is required. :thumbsup:
